claims.text: Set the seat so the shoulders line up with the machine's pivot points (about level with the handles).

quotes.text: Adjust seat height so shoulders align with machine's pivot point.
Adjust the seat height so that your shoulders are level with the handles.

claims.text: Sit with the back against the pad and the feet flat on the floor.

quotes.text: Sit with back against pad, place arms on pads with elbows slightly bent and feet flat on floor.
Keep your feet flat on the floor, shoulder-width apart.

claims.text: Place the arms on the pads, which rest against the arm just above the elbows, and hold the handles.

quotes.text: the pads resting just above the elbows.
Position your forearms under the pads and grip the handles with each hand.
Adjust the machine so that the pads are leaning against your elbows.

claims.text: Raise the arms out to the sides by pressing out through the elbows, leading with the elbows.

quotes.text: lift the pads upward by pressing out through the elbows and raising the upper arms.
Exhale and raise arms outward to sides, leading with elbows.

claims.text: Lift until the upper arms are horizontal, with the elbows level with the shoulders.

quotes.text: Lift your arms out to your sides, until your upper arms are horizontal.
Raise your arms out and away from your sides until your elbows are even with your shoulders, pause, and then reverse the motion.

claims.text: Don't shrug the shoulders up; excessive shrugging lets the trapezius take over.

quotes.text: raise to parallel with floor, avoiding shoulder shrug or overextension.
Avoid excessive shrugging to prevent trap dominance

claims.text: It is easy to pick a weight that is too heavy; err on the lighter side. If you can't raise the elbows to shoulder height, lower the weight.

quotes.text: This is an exercise where it is easy to pick a weight that is too heavy. Rather err on the lighter side, and strive for a strict form where you focus on getting good contact with your delts.
If you can not raise your arms so that your elbows are even with your shoulders lower the weight.

claims.text: Avoid momentum or swinging the body to finish a rep: it makes the exercise less effective and can lead to injury.

quotes.text: Avoid using momentum or swinging your body to complete the exercise, as this reduces the effectiveness and can lead to injury.

claims.text: Lower the arms slowly with control, stopping just before the weight stack rests.

quotes.text: Stop just before the weight stack rests in the original position.
Keep control of the weight as you lower your arms down.

claims.text: Breathe out as the arms lift and in as they lower.

quotes.text: Inhale during lowering phase; exhale as you lift and squeeze at top.

claims.text: The machine lateral raise targets the middle (side) deltoid; across studies, shoulder abduction exercises gave the highest middle deltoid activation (review of mostly free-weight and cable studies).

quotes.text: Machine lateral raise isolates medial deltoids
for middle deltoid, abductions and horizontal abductions presented the greatest activation

claims.text: The trapezius may also work as a secondary muscle.

quotes.text: While the workout may also engage secondary muscles, such as the trapezius and deltoids, its main focus is on the shoulders.

claims.text: Tempo: moderate speed, about 1-2 s each way, with a brief pause at the top.

quotes.text: at a moderate contraction velocity (1-2 s CON; 1-2 s ECC)
Pause briefly at top to squeeze deltoids.

claims.text: Load progression: add 2-10% load once you can do one or two reps more than the target number.

quotes.text: When training at a specific RM load, it is recommended that 2-10% increase in load be applied when the individual can perform the current workload for one to two repetitions over the desired number.

claims.text: On ACE's version you sit facing the machine and keep the elbows bent at 90 degrees.

plate.viewWhy: The arms rise sideways in the frontal plane (c4, c5), which reads only from the front (census: front). The drawn fault, shrugging (c6), also shows from the front.
plate.equipment: Seated lateral raise machine (composed, census R3): seat, back pad, two arm pads on levers pivoting at shoulder height, handles (c1-c3). Floor line.
plate.start: Seated, back on the pad, feet flat (c2); arms at the sides, pads resting just above the elbows, hands on the handles (c3); shoulders level with the pivots (c1).
plate.end: Upper arms horizontal, elbows level with the shoulders (c5); shoulders down, not shrugged (c6); back still on the pad (c2).

mistake.what: Shrugging: the shoulders hike up toward the ears as the arms rise.

tells.text: Shoulders stay down, away from ears
